speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) when was the last revision of the household income eligibility criteria for the Disabled Persons Scheme; and (b) whether the criteria are being evaluated so as to remain relevant amidst inflation and rising costs of living.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In recent years, there have been increasingly more transport options for persons with disabilities who cannot take public transport.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, all taxis are required to be able to fit foldable wheelchairs in their boot.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Taxi and private hire car operators have introduced more wheelchair-accessible vehicles.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The first question is regarding the existing scheme, the DPS.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Do we also consider, as part of the assessment, the upkeep needs of the other dependents within the same household?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: So, for example, if there are very young children, infants who need care, is that a factor considered when there are appeals?
